userStories.title: Incremental Graph Diff — Replace Full Re-Import
acceptanceCriteria: IncrementalGraphDiffService.diffAndApply() computes a diff and applies only the delta
Stored graph is loaded from GraphNode + GraphLink Prisma tables; not from LanceDB
When newNodes has 100 nodes and stored has 90, added=10 and removed=0
When a stored node is absent from newNodes, it is deleted from both GraphNode table and LanceDB (by graphify nodeId / RAG sourceId)
When a node exists in both with unchanged content, it is skipped (no re-index)
diffAndApply is called by the existing importGraphify endpoint (replaces deleteAllBySourceType logic)
DiffResult.indexed reflects only the number of nodes actually written to LanceDB (not total nodes)
A diff-and-apply of 500 unchanged nodes + 10 added + 5 removed completes in under 2 seconds
DiffResult includes durationMs for performance monitoring
Only actors with role admin, developer, or agent can call importGraphify (enforced at controller layer)
suggestedCriteria: When newNodes is empty and stored has nodes, all stored nodes are removed from GraphNode/GraphLink and LanceDB
When projectId does not exist, diffAndApply returns the repo-standard KodaError/Nathapp not-found style
Concurrent diffAndApply calls for the same projectId are serialized or conflict deterministically; no duplicate or torn graph state is persisted
If LanceDB write/delete fails after Prisma diff persistence, the operation marks affected graph rows as pending reindex and returns an error for retry

userStories.title: VCS Webhook Handler → code_commit Outbox Event
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Extend the existing project-scoped VCS webhook surface so push/code-intel events enqueue `code_commit` outbox records instead of doing code indexing synchronously.

**Motivation** — Push webhooks usually contain file names, not full source contents, so the outbox handler must resolve file contents before calling the AST indexer and the controller must stay thin.

**Approach** — The webhook controller stays on `POST /projects/:slug/vcs-webhook`, validates the provider signature with the existing `x-hub-signature-256` flow, verifies the payload has a repository identifier, `ref`, `commits[]`, and sender identifier, and enqueues one `code_commit` outbox event per commit with `{ repoId, commitHash, ref, changedFiles }`. The `code_commit` outbox handler resolves changed file contents before calling `AstIndexService.indexCommit()`. Replaying the same `commitHash` within a 5-minute window must not create duplicate outbox rows.

**Interface** — `VcsWebhookController` continues to own the public webhook route, and the outbox payload for code indexing is `{ repoId, commitHash, ref, changedFiles }`.
acceptanceCriteria: VcsWebhookController extends the existing project-scoped webhook surface at POST /projects/:slug/vcs-webhook to handle push/code-intel events
Webhook payload is validated: presence of repository identifier, ref, commits[], and sender identifier (sender.id, sender.login, or provider equivalent)
For each commit in the push, a code_commit outbox event is enqueued with { repoId, commitHash, ref, changedFiles }
AstIndexService.indexCommit() is called by the code_commit outbox handler, not synchronously by the webhook controller
If event enqueue fails, the webhook logs the failure and returns a non-2xx response so the provider can retry
GitHub webhook signature verification reuses the existing x-hub-signature-256 flow already used by Koda VCS webhooks; invalid signatures return 401
The webhook secret continues to come from the project's VCS connection record (never hard-coded)
Webhook handler is idempotent: pushing the same commitHash twice does not create duplicate outbox events (dedup by commitHash within a 5-minute window)
suggestedCriteria: If webhook signature header is missing, the endpoint returns 401
If project slug is not found, the endpoint returns 404
If commits[] is empty, no code_commit outbox events are created
Outbox dedup key is projectId+repoId+commitHash and is persisted (not in-memory) so retries across restarts remain idempotent
The code_commit handler uses a FileContentProvider interface and enforces per-file timeout with partial-file error recording

userStories.title: AST/Symbol Index Pipeline
acceptanceCriteria: AstIndexService.indexCommit() parses source files and stores symbol metadata in the Symbol Prisma table
Symbol.symbolId uses the convention {repoId}:{filePath}::{SymbolName} and is globally unique within a project
getCallers(symbolId) returns all symbols that include this symbol in their JSON callers list
getCallees(symbolId) returns all symbols in this symbol's JSON callees list
When indexCommit is called with files=[{path: 'src/auth.ts', content: '...'}], only src/auth.ts is parsed (incremental — existing symbols for unchanged files are preserved)
Symbol.signature captures parameter types and return type (e.g. '(userId: string): Promise<User>')
Indexing is triggered by a code_commit outbox event (fired by the VCS webhook handler)
A commit with 20 files (avg 200 lines each) is indexed in under 30 seconds
Only actors with role admin or developer can call AstIndexService.indexCommit() directly (not agents); role checked at controller layer
Parser failures for one file are recorded in the result and do not prevent other files in the same commit from being indexed
The code_commit handler resolves changed file contents before calling indexCommit(); the webhook controller only enqueues commit metadata
suggestedCriteria: When files=[] the result is symbolsIndexed=0 and filesIndexed=0
When symbolId does not exist, getSymbol returns null
When a previously indexed symbol is removed from a changed file, it is marked inactive/deleted so getCallers/getCallees and impact queries do not return stale active symbols
Concurrent indexCommit executions for the same project/repo use deterministic upsert semantics on Symbol(projectId,symbolId)
Parser timeouts and syntax errors are recorded in fileErrors with path and message, while successful files remain committed

userStories.title: Ticket/Entity Graph Builder
acceptanceCriteria: EntityGraphService.rebuildGraph(projectId) rebuilds all entity nodes and links for a project
Entity graph data is persisted in EntityNode and EntityLink tables, not only in Phase 2's in-memory EntityStore
onTicketEvent(status_changed) updates the entity node for that ticket (if it exists)
onGraphifyImport() extracts service entities from graphify nodes with type=code_module

The initial implementation does not require a Ticket.serviceId column; service linkage works from current Koda fields (gitRefFile, labels, linked code/module references) until an explicit service relation exists
getRelatedEntities(projectId, entityId, depth=2) returns all entities reachable within 2 hops
getIncidentImpact(projectId, incidentTicketId) returns all entities linked to the incident
Service entities extracted from graphify inherit tags from the graphify node (e.g. ['backend', 'auth'])
Entity graph is updated incrementally via outbox fan-out (no full rebuild on every event)
A graph with 500 nodes and 2000 edges returns getRelatedEntities in under 50ms
suggestedCriteria: getRelatedEntities is cycle-safe and does not loop infinitely on cyclic service dependencies
If entityId does not exist in the project, getRelatedEntities returns an empty array
Soft-deleted tickets/services are excluded from traversal and incident impact unless explicitly requested for historical mode
Service linkage inference uses deterministic rule priority (gitRefFile exact/prefix match, then graph source_file match, then label match, then unclassified fallback)
Repeated ticket or graphify events are idempotent and do not create duplicate EntityNode/EntityLink rows

userStories.title: getChangeImpact API
acceptanceCriteria: GET /projects/:slug/codeintel/impact?repoId=X&commitHash=Y&changedFiles=file1,file2 returns a ChangeImpactResult
impactedSymbols contains symbols whose file matches any entry in changedFiles
impactedServices contains service entities linked to impacted symbols through matching Symbol.file → GraphNode.sourceFile or EntityNode.sourceId
impactedTickets contains tickets linked to any impactedServices
impactScore is a number 0-100 computed by the formula in the design section
When called with a ticketId, the result includes provenance source metadata pointing to that ticket
The endpoint returns in under 5 seconds for a commit touching up to 50 files
Only actors with role admin, developer, or agent can call this endpoint (role checked at controller level)
suggestedCriteria: When changedFiles is empty, impactScore is 0 and impactedSymbols/impactedServices/impactedTickets are empty arrays
When all relevant denominators are zero, each weighted term contributes 0 and the final score is 0
The endpoint enforces a max response size or pagination for impactedSymbols to prevent oversized payloads
Project-level authorization is enforced in addition to role checks (caller must have access to the target project slug)

userStories.title: CanonicalStateService Snapshot Read Layer
acceptanceCriteria: CanonicalStateService.getSnapshot(query) returns retrievedAt set to the server timestamp
When ticketIds are provided, tickets contains only tickets in the requested projectId
When timeWindow is provided, recentEvents contains only events in the window, ordered by createdAt DESC
activeDecisions is populated from active MemoryItem rows with kind='DECISION'
A non-existent or unauthorized projectId throws the same KodaError/Nathapp exception style used by earlier memory endpoints
The service performs canonical Prisma reads only; it does not query LanceDB, BM25, entity graph, or other derived stores
suggestedCriteria: If timeWindow.from is after timeWindow.to, the service returns a validation error
Soft-deleted tickets are excluded from tickets in snapshot results
If no active decisions exist, activeDecisions returns an empty array
The definition of active decisions is explicit and testable (e.g., status flag or equivalent query predicate), not inferred implicitly from kind alone

analysis: Phase 4 will be implemented as an incremental migration on top of existing Koda seams (graphify import, outbox fan-out, VCS webhook surface, and project-scoped graphify controls). The core objective is a deterministic, project-isolated foundation: durable graph persistence, incremental diff ingestion, parser-derived symbol indexing, durable entity graph traversal, and change-impact querying. Prisma is the source of truth; LanceDB remains derived and recoverable. This synthesis keeps the spec’s required interfaces and acceptance criteria, while adding hardening criteria for idempotency, cycle safety, soft-delete behavior, concurrent processing, and file-content resolution reliability.
